topic: Capacity expansion to 10.4 bcm/y (approval and phased commissioning)
wiki_text: On 16 April 2025 the Italian government approved, by decree, an 8% increase in the regasification capacity of the Adriatic LNG terminal, from 9.6 to 10.4 billion cubic metres per year. To implement it, Adriatic LNG shut the offshore terminal on 1 August 2025 for scheduled maintenance and plant modifications. The first phase raised constant regasification capacity from 9 to 9.5 bcm/y around 31 December 2025, with the full incremental capacity (0.5 bcm/y allocated via open season from January 2026) available in the first quarter of 2026. In 2024 the terminal had set an operational record, sending out 8.7 bcm of gas (about 15% of national demand).

wiki_text: Snam's Ravenna FSRU, using the 170,000-cbm 2015-built vessel BW Singapore (5 bcm/y regasification capacity) moored about 8.5 km offshore Ravenna, completed commissioning on schedule in April 2025 and began commercial regasification in May 2025. With its entry into service, Italy's total LNG regasification capacity rose to roughly 28 bcm/y. The terminal has been operational since May 2025 and Snam continued to offer Ravenna regasification capacity into 2026.
